units.title: Unit 53 — Phoning and texting
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 53. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Open informal and formal telephone calls with natural British English phrases.
Identify callers, request to speak to somebody and transfer a call politely.
Explain telephone problems, busy lines, missed contacts and return calls.
Distinguish mobile, home, emergency and international dialling numbers.
Recognise common texting abbreviations and their full expressions.

items.example: My brother answered the phone while I was cooking.
items.note: Respond when the telephone rings.

items.pt: É o Joe?; estou falando com o Joe?
items.example: She asked, "Is that Joe?" when someone picked up.
items.note: A natural informal way to check the identity of the person answering in British English.

items.pt: É a Lily; aqui é a Lily.
items.example: When her friend answered, Lily said, "Hi, it's Lily."
items.note: Use It's followed by your name to identify yourself on a personal call; not I am Lily in this context.

items.word: Could I speak to Jane, please?
items.pt: Eu poderia falar com a Jane, por favor?
items.example: I asked, "Could I speak to Jane, please?"
items.note: Polite request to speak to another person; substitute any name.

items.example: The receptionist asked, "Who's calling, please?"
items.note: Formal telephone question asking for the caller's identity.

items.example: The caller said, "My name is Paul," before asking for the manager.
items.note: A suitable way to introduce yourself on a business call; replace Paul with your own name.

items.example: The receptionist put me through to the accounts department.
items.note: Connect a caller to another person or telephone extension; also put someone through to someone.

items.example: Please hold; I'm putting you through now.
items.note: A receptionist says this while connecting a call.

items.pt: É ele(a) quem fala; sou eu.
items.example: When I asked for Ms Brown, she replied, "Speaking."
items.note: A conventional answer when somebody asks to speak to you by name.

items.pt: Estou falando com o Sr. James?
items.example: I asked, "Is that Mr James?" after the call was connected.
items.note: Use Is that plus a name to check who is on the phone.

items.example: One moment, please; I'll check whether she's available.
items.note: A polite request to wait during a phone conversation.

items.example: I'll ring my sister after dinner.
items.note: Common British English verb for telephone someone; past tense rang.

items.example: I phoned the office twice this morning.
items.note: Verb phone is normally used without to before the person.

items.example: Could you call me when you arrive?
items.note: An alternative to phone or ring someone.

items.example: Give me a ring when you have a minute.
items.note: Informal phrase meaning make a telephone call.

items.example: I couldn't talk because I was on the phone.
items.note: Describes somebody already using a telephone.

items.example: I dialled the number again to check it.
items.note: Enter a telephone number in order to call.

items.example: Sorry, I think you've got the wrong number.
items.note: The number you called does not reach the person intended.

items.pt: conseguir completar a ligação; conseguir falar ao telefone
items.example: I tried several times but couldn't get through.
items.note: Make telephone contact successfully; often used with to.

items.pt: conseguir falar com alguém por telefone
items.example: I finally got through to the customer service team.
items.note: Use get through to plus the person or organisation contacted.

items.example: The line was engaged, so I called back later.
items.note: In British English, an engaged line is already in use; US English often uses busy.

items.example: I couldn't reach him because the line was engaged.
items.note: A common phrase for an unsuccessful call caused by another conversation.

items.pt: deixar um recado; deixar uma mensagem
items.example: I left a message asking her to call me.
items.note: Record or pass information when the person cannot answer.

items.example: Her answerphone picked up after six rings.
items.note: British English word for a system that records voice messages.

items.pt: ausente; fora de casa ou do escritório
items.example: I'm afraid Mr White is out at the moment.
items.note: Here out means not present or available, rather than outside a building.

items.example: She's not in right now; can I take a message?
items.note: Alternative to out when the person is not present.

items.example: I'll phone you back as soon as the meeting ends.
items.note: Return a telephone call; ring back or call back also work.

items.example: Could you call me back in an hour?
items.note: Separable phrasal verb: call her back, not call back her.

items.example: Can I take a message while he's away?
items.note: A conventional offer to record a caller's message.

items.example: Our home phone number has changed.
items.note: The number of a telephone at home, usually a landline.

items.example: We still have a landline at the office.
items.note: A fixed telephone connection rather than a mobile phone.

items.example: Please write your mobile number on the form.
items.note: A mobile phone number; the source uses British English mobile.

items.example: Do you know the local emergency number?
items.note: Telephone number for urgent services such as fire, police or ambulance.

items.example: Check the international dialling code before calling abroad.
items.note: Digits used before a number for a particular country or area; British spelling dialling.

items.example: I mainly use my phone for messages.
items.note: Mostly; most of the time.

items.pt: na maior parte do tempo; principalmente
items.example: I mostly text rather than make calls.
items.note: Similar in meaning to mainly.

items.example: I'll text you the address later.
items.note: Verb meaning send a short written message by phone.

items.pt: troca de mensagens de texto; envio de SMS
items.example: Texting is convenient when someone can't answer a call.
items.note: The activity of exchanging short phone messages.

items.example: LOL is a common abbreviation in messages.
items.note: A shortened written form of a word or phrase.

items.pt: o quanto antes; assim que possível
items.example: Please send the details ASAP.
items.note: Text abbreviation for as soon as possible; may be spoken as letters or as a word.

items.example: She mentioned her BF in the message.
items.note: Text shorthand for boyfriend, not a standard spoken noun.

items.example: He said he was meeting his GF after work.
items.note: Text shorthand for girlfriend.

items.example: I've seen that film B4.
items.note: Text shorthand for before; the numeral represents a sound in the word.

items.example: Are you free 2DAY?
items.note: Text shorthand for today; not standard formal writing.

items.example: I'll let you know 2MORO.
items.note: Text shorthand for tomorrow as presented in the source.

items.example: Y are you leaving early?
items.note: Text shorthand for why, normally followed by a question.

items.example: PLS call me when you arrive.
items.note: Text shorthand for please.

items.example: See you later: CU!
items.note: Text shorthand for see you; use only in casual messages.

items.example: IMO, the second option is better.
items.note: Text abbreviation for in my opinion.

items.example: FYI, the deadline has changed.
items.note: Text abbreviation for for your information; often used in email as well.

items.example: How are U?
items.note: Text shorthand for you; very informal.

items.example: THX for your help!
items.note: Text shorthand for thanks.

items.example: That was hilarious, LOL!
items.note: Text abbreviation for laughing out loud; often signals amusement.

items.example: She signed her message with an X.
items.note: A written X often stands for a kiss at the end of informal messages.

items.example: GRT! I'll see you there.
items.note: Exercise-only texting shorthand for great; extremely informal.

sectionsChecked: A: Starting a phone conversation; informal and business dialogues and common-mistake box
B: Problems on the phone; phone, dial, engaged line, answerphone and return calls
C: Phone numbers; home/landline, mobile, emergency and international dialling code
D: Mobile phones and texting; abbreviations and full forms
Exercises 53.1–53.4 and Unit 53 answer key; contact phrases, dialogue completion and abbreviations

units.title: Unit 54 — Computers
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 54. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Name major computer parts and common peripheral devices.
Follow basic steps for signing in, opening, editing, saving and printing documents.
Distinguish backup the noun from back up the verb and describe a system crash.
Describe hardware, an operating system, installed applications and computer security.
Use correct word partnerships involving files, drives, passwords and software.

items.example: She switched on her webcam for the online meeting.
items.note: A small camera connected to or built into a computer.

items.example: The figures are too small to read on this screen.
items.note: The part of a computer that displays images and text.

items.example: The office printer has run out of paper.
items.note: A machine that produces text or pictures on paper.

items.example: The old program came on a CD-ROM.
items.note: A disc used for storing or distributing computer data; a legacy format.

items.example: Check that your microphone works before joining the call.
items.note: An input device that records sound.

items.example: Press the Escape key to close the menu.
items.note: A keyboard key often labelled Esc.

items.example: Use the spacebar to put spaces between words.
items.note: The long key that inserts a space.

items.example: I prefer an external keyboard for typing.
items.note: A set of keys used to enter text and commands.

items.example: My mouse moves smoothly across this mouse mat.
items.note: British English term for a pad under a computer mouse.

items.example: Move the mouse to the top-right corner.
items.note: A pointing device used to control the cursor.

items.pt: pen drive; unidade USB de armazenamento
items.example: I copied the presentation onto a memory stick.
items.note: A small portable device for storing computer files.

items.example: Switch on the computer before the training starts.
items.note: Turn on and start the machine; the phrasal verb switch on is separable.

items.example: Turn on your computer and open the browser.
items.note: Synonym for switch on; turn it on with a pronoun.

items.example: You need to log in before opening your files.
items.note: Sign in to an account or system; also log on.

items.example: Log on with your usual credentials.
items.note: Alternative to log in; often followed by to plus a system.

items.example: Remember to log out when you finish.
items.note: End a signed-in session; the opposite of log in.

items.example: She logged off the shared computer.
items.note: Alternative to log out; often followed by from or a direct system object.

items.example: Enter your username in the first field.
items.note: The name used to identify an account.

items.example: Never share your password with anyone.
items.note: A secret value used to gain access to a system.

items.example: Enter your password to unlock the laptop.
items.note: Type a password into a login field.

items.example: Double-click the icon to open the program.
items.note: Click a mouse button twice quickly.

items.example: Click the folder icon on the screen.
items.note: A small image representing a file, command or application.

items.example: This application helps us organise documents.
items.note: Software designed to do a particular task.

items.example: The database stores information about every order.
items.note: Keep information in computer storage for later use.

items.pt: fazer cópia de segurança dos arquivos
items.example: Back up your files before installing an update.
items.note: Verb phrase: make an extra copy to prevent data loss.

items.example: I made a backup before changing the settings.
items.note: Noun: an extra copy kept for recovery; compare the verb back up.

items.example: The file is too large to email.
items.note: A collection of computer data saved under a name.

items.example: Open a new document to write your report.
items.note: Start a blank document in an application.

items.example: Open an existing document to correct the figures.
items.note: Access a document that has already been saved.

items.example: Save the document before closing the application.
items.note: Write document changes to storage.

items.example: Please print the document for the meeting.
items.note: Produce a paper version of a digital document.

items.example: Cut the paragraph and move it to the last page.
items.note: Editing command that removes selected content so it can be pasted elsewhere.

items.example: Copy the text into the new file.
items.note: Editing command that duplicates selected content without removing the original.

items.example: Paste the copied address into the form.
items.note: Insert content previously cut or copied.

items.example: You can copy and paste the table into your email.
items.note: A common pair of editing actions.

items.example: Create a document for the meeting notes.
items.note: Make a new file or document.

items.example: Select New from the File menu.
items.note: A menu in many applications containing commands for documents.

items.pt: imprimir; produzir uma cópia em papel
items.example: You can print out the timetable later.
items.note: Separable phrasal verb: print it out.

items.example: Could I have a hard copy of the contract?
items.note: A physical printed version of a digital document.

items.example: The printout is on your desk.
items.note: Noun for a sheet or document produced by a printer.

items.example: My computer crashed before I saved the changes.
items.note: A computer or application crash is a sudden failure.

items.example: Press the Escape key to leave the menu.
items.note: Common keyboard instruction for stopping or cancelling an action.

items.example: Exit the application when you are finished.
items.note: Close or stop using a software application.

items.example: The FAQ explains how to reset a password.
items.note: FAQ stands for frequently asked question; FAQs is its plural.

items.example: Our new PC has a much larger screen.
items.note: Abbreviation for personal computer.

items.example: A personal computer is suitable for everyday office work.
items.note: Full term behind the abbreviation PC.

items.example: I take my laptop to the office every day.
items.note: A portable computer with a built-in keyboard and screen.

items.example: The hard drive stores all the project files.
items.note: Storage hardware in a computer; also hard disk in the source.

items.example: The old laptop has a small hard disk.
items.note: Alternative source term for hard drive.

items.example: The operating system manages the computer's resources.
items.note: Core software that controls the computer's operation.

items.example: We need special software to analyse these files.
items.note: Uncountable noun for computer programs; not a software in this sense.

items.example: Install the software before starting the course.
items.note: Put a program on a computer so it can be used.

items.pt: executar um aplicativo; utilizar um programa
items.example: My laptop can run several applications at once.
items.note: Here run means use or execute a program, not move quickly.

items.example: A computer virus damaged some of the saved files.
items.note: A malicious program that can disrupt or harm data.

items.example: Keep your anti-virus software up to date.
items.note: Software designed to detect or block computer viruses; uncountable software.

sectionsChecked: A: The computer; labelled illustration of input, output and storage devices
B: Using a computer; sign-in, application launch, storage, backup, document commands and crash
C: FAQs about computers; PC, laptop, hard disk, operating system, installations and viruses
Exercises 54.1–54.6 and Unit 54 answer key; hardware compounds, icons, definitions and dialogues
